candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — disaster/surge resource management
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize the major operational domains that must be addressed during health-care surge planning.

options.A: Address space, staff, supplies/stuff, and systems together as demand increases.
options.B: Increase bed count only; staffing and supplies can be addressed after the surge ends.
options.C: Focus only on medication inventory because systems and staffing do not affect capacity.
options.D: Suspend coordination structures so each department can respond independently.

candidate.rationale: ASPR TRACIE surge-capacity guidance describes the need to address the interdependent domains of space, staff, stuff/supplies, and systems when expanding capacity.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Health-care surge capacity requires coordinated planning for space, staff, supplies/stuff, and systems.
candidate.source_document_title: Healthcare System Considerations for Surge Capacity and Crisis Standards of Care
candidate.source_locator: Surge concepts — Space, Staff, Stuff, Systems
candidate.source_organization: Administration for Strategic Preparedness and Response (ASPR) TRACIE
candidate.stem: During a sudden patient surge, which planning framework best reflects ASPR TRACIE guidance for expanding health-care capacity?
